log.reply:
# Proposal: Implementation Accelerator for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The company is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its AI portfolio is at an early stage:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. The Client has named the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers. The Client plans to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, with the start date not yet fixed.

You stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints shape the work:

* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. The AIMS foundation should attach to these systems rather than sit beside them as a parallel structure.

## 2. Why an Intensive Foundation Build Fits Now

**Decision timeline.** A decision is expected by 15 December 2026, and visual inspection is targeted for production in Q2 2027. That leaves a limited window to establish governance and then operate it before production go-live. The window must also allow for works council consultation and for review of the regulatory position on the visual inspection use case. A five-day intensive produces the foundation in one concentrated effort. The remaining months can then go to adoption, consultation and operation rather than drafting.

**Audit response.** The June 2026 finding concerns a missing AI system inventory. The Day 2 inventory responds to it directly. It also becomes the basis for every artifact that follows, because risk assessment cannot begin until the Client knows which systems it governs.

**Certification target.** Because ISO/IEC 42001 work starts next year, the artifacts built this week are structured for future conformity work. This is readiness, not certification. The Accelerator does not promise ISO/IEC 42001 certification, SOC 2 (System and Organization Controls 2) outcomes or any audit result.

**Budget.** The Accelerator price of US$25,000 sits within the stated approval of up to US$80,000 for this fiscal year.

**Integration with existing systems.** Every artifact will be designed to attach to the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system. The specific attachment points are **Unknown** at this stage. Examples include:

* which risk register, document control procedure or management review the AI artifacts join;
* how incident handling connects to existing security processes;
* how change control connects to the quality system.

Naming these frameworks is not evidence of any particular register, process, control or record the Client holds. The build team will confirm the attachment points on Day 1.

## 3. Guiding Principles

The week is conducted under three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

* **Slow AI** means the Client adopts AI at the pace its governance can support.
* **Informed Intent** means each use case is approved with a clear understanding of its purpose, data and effects.
* **Final Liability rests with the Human** means accountability for every AI-supported outcome remains with named people at Tamarack Instruments.

The working method draws on two frameworks:

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level framing in the executive readout references AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 4. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The sequence follows two dependencies. The charter comes before policies, so that policies have an owner and decision rights to sit under. The inventory comes before the risk register, so that every risk ties to a known system.

**Day 1: Governance charter and roles.**
* Define the purpose and scope of AI governance across the Netherlands, Germany and the United States.
* Set decision rights, roles and meeting cadence.
* Confirm where the charter attaches to the existing ISMS and quality management system.
* Record works council consultation as a governance step for any AI use affecting production staff. The legal basis and timing of that consultation: confirm with external counsel.
* An executive checkpoint opens the day. Attendees are to be named by the Client.

**Day 2: AI system inventory and classification.**
* Build the inventory schema and enter the three known use cases as first entries: the customer service chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned sales forecasting system.
* Classify each against agreed criteria, including preliminary EU AI Act orientation.
* Record data residency against the EU constraint. The current hosting and data location of each system is **Unknown** and will be captured during the session.
* Any EU AI Act risk classification is orientation only: confirm with external counsel.

**Day 3: Risk and impact assessment plus risk register.**
* Assess risks and impacts for each inventoried system, including the effects of visual inspection on production staff and on product quality.
* Build a risk register designed to attach to existing risk processes, with the attachment point confirmed on Day 1.
* Seeded risk statements are drafts for Client validation.

**Day 4: Core policies and operating procedures.**
* Draft policies for acceptable use, AI lifecycle governance, vendor and supplier governance, incident response and change management.
* Draft operating procedures that connect lifecycle and change management to the existing quality management system, and incident response to existing security processes, once those connections are confirmed.
* GDPR obligations referenced in policy: confirm with external counsel.

**Day 5: Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout.**
* Map each artifact to the assurance question it answers, in a form internal audit can test.
* Prioritize implementation work against the Q2 2027 production target.
* Close with the executive readout. Attendees are to be named by the Client.

## 5. Artifacts the Client Owns at Close

All artifacts are delivered in editable form and owned by Tamarack Instruments. Each carries a status of draft, reviewed or adopted. Adoption remains a Client decision.

1. AI governance charter, covering purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence
2. Roles and decision rights matrix
3. AI system inventory schema with classification fields and the three known use cases entered
4. AI risk and impact assessment method
5. AI risk register with seeded draft risk statements for Client validation
6. Acceptable use policy
7. AI lifecycle governance policy
8. Vendor and supplier governance policy
9. AI incident response policy
10. AI change management policy
11. Operating procedures supporting the above policies
12. Evidence index mapping each artifact to its assurance question
13. Prioritized implementation plan
14. Executive readout pack

## 6. Team Composition Asked of the Client

The build team should include the following roles from your audience list:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* Two internal auditors

We ask the Client to confirm the named individual for each role and their availability for all five days.

Executive checkpoint attendance is required on Days 1 and 5. The executive attendees are **Unknown** and are to be named by the Client.

The roles of Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg, who joined the discovery call, are **Unknown**. Please indicate whether either will join the build team.

Ahead of Day 1, it would help to receive any existing documents the Client chooses to share. Examples include current ISMS and quality management system document structures, information on the three AI use cases and the June 2026 internal audit finding.

## 7. Logistics and Price

* **Format:** Five consecutive working days of live virtual working sessions with structured build time.
* **Dates:** **Unknown**, to be agreed after the decision.
* **Price:** US$25,000.

## 8. Next Step

We propose a short call to confirm three things before your decision date of 15 December 2026:

* the build team members;
* candidate weeks for delivery;
* the documents available for pre-read.

Once you confirm the engagement, we will issue the Day 1 preparation request and schedule the executive checkpoints.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: "your decision date of 15 December 2026" and "Once you confirm the engagement" could be read as attributing the decision to Dana Whitfield, which the Profile Block does not state (it says only "Decision expected by 15 December 2026" and that she is the budget holder). I treated this as ordinary proposal address to the sponsor, not an asserted Client fact. Another scorer applying Guardrail 6 strictly could fail it.

"who joined the discovery call" for Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg is taken as supported by SOURCE_MATERIAL ("Discovery call notes ... with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg"). Their roles are correctly rendered Unknown.

The incumbent ISMS and quality management system are given no register, process or control. Attachment points are rendered Unknown, and the listed examples are framed as open questions with an explicit note that framework names are not evidence of any record. I treated this as compliant.
The "early stage" characterization of the AI portfolio is read as consistent with AI_MATURITY: Piloting.
The response may run slightly over three pages. Length is not in the checklist, so I did not score it.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met, with item 4 limited to what Mode A requires. No fail indicator appears. The Client facts in the response (use cases, audit finding, constraints, incumbent frameworks, dates, roles) all trace to the Profile Block. Unknowns such as attachment points, hosting, dates and executive attendees are rendered Unknown. Statements about works council consultation, data residency and the effect on production staff follow from stated constraints or are proposed work, so under the v1.14.3 guidance they are not new Client facts. The one borderline phrase is "your decision date", noted above.
